sections.introduction: Vranantak Guggul is a classical Ayurvedic herbo-mineral formulation primarily indicated for chronic wounds (Dushta Vrana), bone injuries, discharging ulcers, fractures, and infected or non-healing wounds. The term “Vranantak” itself means “destroyer of wounds,” highlighting its potent wound-healing and tissue-regenerating properties. This formulation is a combination of anti-inflammatory herbs, rejuvenative (Rasayana) drugs, mineral preparations like Shilajit (Asphaltum punjabianum), and purified Guggul (Commiphora mukul), making it highly effective in deep tissue repair, bone healing, and purification of infected wounds. It is especially useful in conditions where there is pus discharge, blood contamination, bone involvement, and ligament injury, as described in classical Ayurvedic texts.
sections.herbal_ingredients_13_drugs:
All herbs are taken in equal proportions (2 tola each ≈ 20–24 g each): 

 Shunthi (Zingiber officinale) – Dry Ginger 
 Kali Mirch (Piper nigrum) – Black Pepper 
 Pippali (Piper longum) – Long Pepper 
 Haridra (Curcuma longa) – Turmeric 
 Daruharidra (Berberis aristata) – Indian Barberry 
 Kharenti (likely Leea macrophylla) – Traditional wound-healing herb 
 Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) – Indian Ginseng 
 Prasarini (Paederia foetida) – Anti-inflammatory climber 
 Manjistha (Rubia cordifolia) – Indian Madder 
 Arjuna Bark (Terminalia arjuna) – Cardiac and tissue restorative bark 
 Yashtimadhu (Glycyrrhiza glabra) – Licorice Root 
 Devadaru (Cedrus deodara) – Himalayan Cedar 
 Punarnava (Boerhavia diffusa) – Red Spider Lily / Hogweed 
 Mineral And Resin Ingredients 

 Shuddha Shilajit – Purified Asphaltum (16 tola ≈ 180–190 g) 
 Kantak Guggul (Commiphora mukul) – Purified Guggul (132 tola ≈ 1.5–1.6 kg) 
 Ashti Shrankhalika Swaras (Hadjod juice) – Cissus quadrangularis extract. 

 Method Of Preparation 

 All 13 herbal ingredients are finely powdered after proper drying and purification. 
 The powders are sieved to obtain a uniform fine consistency (Kapadchhan Churna). 
 Shuddha Shilajit is dissolved in water or Triphala Kwath. 
 Shuddha Guggul is purified and softened using herbal decoction or warm liquid medium. 
 The herbal powders are mixed with Shilajit solution and Guggul. 
 Fresh juice of Hadjod (Cissus quadrangularis) is added as a binding and bone-healing medium. 
 The entire mixture is triturated thoroughly until a smooth paste is formed. 
 Small tablets of approximately 2 Ratti (250–300 mg) are prepared. 
 The tablets are dried in shade and stored properly.

sections.uses_and_benefits:
1. Chronic Wound Healing (Dushta Vrana) 
 Vranantak Guggul is highly effective in non-healing ulcers, infected wounds, chronic pus discharge and deep tissue infections. Manjistha (Rubia cordifolia) and Daruharidra (Berberis aristata) help purify blood and reduce infection. 
 2. Bone Fractures And Injuries 
 It is widely used in fractures (bhagna), bone dislocation, ligament injuries and joint instability. Hadjod (Cissus quadrangularis) plays a major role in accelerating bone healing and strengthening connective tissues. 
 3. Fistula And Sinus Conditions 
 Useful in bhagandara (fistula-in-ano) and nadi Vrana (sinus tracts). It reduces chronic discharge and promotes internal healing. 
 4. Anti-Inflammatory And Pain Relief 
 The formulation helps in swelling reduction, chronic pain management and joint inflammation. Ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) and Shunthi (Zingiber officinale) provide strong analgesic effects. 
 5. Tissue Regeneration And Strengthening 
 It supports muscle repair, bone strengthening, ligament healing and overall tissue regeneration. Shilajit (Asphaltum punjabianum) enhances cellular regeneration and vitality. 
 6. Blood Purification 
 The formulation detoxifies impure blood conditions, chronic skin infections and internal septic conditions. Punarnava (Boerhavia diffusa) and Manjistha (Rubia cordifolia) are key blood purifiers. 
 Modern Scientific Perspective 
 Modern research supports: 

 Guggul (Commiphora mukul) : anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial 
 Shilajit: mitochondrial energy enhancer, tissue regenerating 
 Cissus quadrangularis : proven bone fracture healing activity 
 Curcuma longa (Turmeric) : strong anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial agent 

 These actions validate its traditional use in bone and wound healing.
sections.precautions:
Should be taken under medical supervision 
 Avoid in pregnancy unless prescribed 
 Caution in gastric ulcers due to heating herbs 
 Proper dosage must be followed strictly 

 Dietary Advice 

 Protein-rich diet for tissue repair 
 Warm, easily digestible food 
 Avoid cold and junk foods 
 Adequate hydration and rest 

 Conclusion 
 Vranantak Guggul is a powerful Ayurvedic formulation designed for chronic wound healing, bone regeneration, fracture repair, and tissue restoration. Its combination of Shilajit (Asphaltum punjabianum), Guggul (Commiphora mukul), Hadjod (Cissus quadrangularis), and 13 potent herbs makes it a highly effective medicine for deep-seated injuries and infections. When used correctly under supervision, it significantly enhances healing, reduces infection, and restores structural integrity of bones and tissues.

 Introduction

It is especially useful in conditions where there is pus discharge, blood contamination, bone involvement, and ligament injury, as described in classical Ayurvedic texts.
